text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs and his Finnish counterpart Tarya Karin Halonen will sign an agreement on visa-free travel between Latvia and Finland today. Latvia will sign a similar agreement with Sweden at the beginning of August.

- The Latvian and Russian branches of Inerpol have discovered 85 cars stolen in Latvia, 28 which were stolen in other countries. A new car in Latvia is stolen every four hours, interior ministry spokesman Normunds Belskis said.
- Deputy chairman of Fatherland and Freedom/ LNNK, Juris Dobelis, said the composition of the cabinet in the new government will be unchanged.
- Seventeen ministers were dismissed during the 19 month premiership of Andris Shkele.
- The council of the Union of Christian Democrats decided to participate in the formation of the new government.
- About 13 percent of Latvian citizens have not replaced the old soviet passports which become invalid on November 1.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele will resign today. He will discharge his duties until the new government is formed.
- The sale price of the state's shares in LaSam, a pipeline operator, will remain unchanged, but some changes may occur in the initial balance of Ventspils Nafta after its merger with LaSam.
